beta_new: Climb the corner, then at its top step right and go up to the belay bolts.
Pull onto the ledge from its left end (the crux), then ascend the face's left portion, keeping away from the line of bolts.
Take the previous route up to about two-thirds height, then angle up and right into a crack that goes by a fixed pin and a bolt.
Ascend a chute, clipping a bolt on the way to a shelf, then continue on twin cracks.
Angle leftward and upward onto a horizontal dike, track it to the left, and then a line of bolts climbs directly up the wall.
Climb to the lowest bolt on the neighboring route, then trend up and rightward to a crack that drops from the top.
Dynamic, reachy face moves lead into a roof crack that crosses several stacked ceilings; the sequences are strenuous and a single large cam must go in under the roof ahead of the lip clip.
Clip the bolt, then step into the patina cracks and follow them upward.
Follow the crack as it slants left to the notch, then continue on gentle face, clipping one bolt.
Begin beside Prisoner of Inertia, in or by a corner shaped like an open book; two bolts lead to a pillar crest and one more takes you to the summit.
Boulder by a bolt just beyond the neighboring route to reach a crack that heads right, then returns left to join Squat Rockets.

moves.from: Large cams in the 3 and 4 sizes protect the crack.

value.text: Large cams in the 3 and 4 sizes.

beta_new: Work up a steep groove protected by three bolts.
Use opposing cracks to reach a small ledge, then angle up and rightward on the face, clipping bolts, until you join Easy Day.
Begin over on the southwest wall's leftmost part, clip a bolt and gain a dike holding a fixed pin; keep climbing to a ledge, then finish on the upper wall, which has three bolts.
Begin from the ledge and follow four bolts beside the roof's left margin, in an airy position.

Begin beyond the overhanging base and traverse up and rightward past a bolt, then ascend the chimney in a long first lead of 140 feet with two more bolts, ending on a ledge with belay bolts; a shorter second lead finishes the chimney.
Climb a corner that faces right, clipping three bolts, then move right and continue up a crack with a further two bolts until you top out.
Start in the crack on the north face's right side, then continue directly up, clipping the bolt.

Start a few feet beyond the two earlier routes, pass through the overhang clipping two bolts and reaching a third beside the thin seam; from there either go straight up for the harder finish, or trend right for the easier one.
Leave the notch, clip the bolt, and move into the crack above.
Climb the crack to the arete and carry on up its edge, clipping its two bolts.
Clip the bolts at the start, then enter the thin left-slanting crack.

Go up a steep, enclosed waterchute to a ledge, then work a short face with bolts to a second ledge holding a tree and belay there to cut rope drag. Above, take the corner facing right (the original line and the crux, three bolts) or its twin facing left with cams, then scramble easily rightward.
Steep face moves on the northeast side of a big boulder, protected by two bolts.
Begin on the buttress's left part, clip a pair of bolts, then follow the arching crack and corner past the fixed pieces.
Thin cracks lead to a bolt, and a second bolt sits just beneath the top.
Start next to the ugly chimney and follow cracks that come and go, ending at a rappel anchor.
Follow a slim crack to the finish of a horizontal feature, traverse leftward, then go up with two bolts; a direct start also exists that makes it independent of its neighbor.
Getting the second bolt clipped is the key to the lead; the face above is slabby with few holds.
Follow the chimney, clipping the lone bolt at about mid-height.
Follow the chute past its bolts and fixed pin; shifting rightward at the final bolt makes the climbing easier.
The first pair of bolts are normally prepared in advance from the boulder sitting at the foot, with the rope left hanging from the first.
The crack begins as a seam. Starting off a bolt to the right is possible, but the direct start is easier, though it gives less protection.
Step off the boulder and head straight up to the anchors, keeping to the left of a pine branch.
Climb a crack that leans left from the ledges where the walk ends, then follow a line trending leftward past seven bolts.
Follow the neighboring route Omega through its overhanging crux, then meander right and upward past several bolts.
Above the bivy ledge, use the inside corner that faces left, rising from the ledge's center, then climb the face straight above.
Follow the crack beside My Three Friends until the two nearly meet, then step right and climb a slot past bushes, and finish by moving left to the Stemski rappel.
Branch off The Flake close to the end of its first pitch, heading rightward and then upward, clipping a bolt on the way to the ledge capping the flake.
